items.title: Barry Harris — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: there was a – there was a trumpet player – he’s still around, too, Bobby Rogovin, he had a good ear. And so... he started playing them right back at me.

ctx.x: So now, how does your choir life, with the choirs that you’ve had. How – what’s the history of that?
That’s just – that came from the jazz culture theater. See, I had – I started singing classes. See, I had horn classes, I had singing classes. I couldn’t sing, I couldn’t even

hum phrases for them to be able to get them, you know. When I noticed a change was when there was a – there was a trumpet player – he’s still around, too, Bobby Rogovin, he had a good ear. And so, maybe in my second year or something, in my third year or something. I started singing the phrases, and he started playing them right back at me. I said, “aha!” See, so I knew that I improved there, you know? And then dealing with the singers – learning lyrics, teaching singing, teaching phasing and stuff, you learn…
